regime.label: Hawkish-hold Fed + AI capex bifurcation
regime.note: The 7/29 FOMC held at 3.50-3.75% but drew THREE dissents (Hammack, Kashkari, Logan) voting to RAISE by 25bp, citing inflation still above 2% partly on Middle East energy. The tape sold off hard on it (Dow -2.19%, its worst day since April 2025; Nasdaq closed >10% off its all-time high). Then on 7/30 the market rebounded (SPY +1.68% to 741.71) on a very specific signal: it stopped taxing AI capex uniformly and started discriminating between capex that shows a return and capex that does not. MSFT (+15.61% on 3.4x average volume) reported Azure +43% with annual Azure revenue over $100B and guided Q1 FY27 Azure to ~45% cc; META (-7.95%) reported EPS $6.18 against $7.14 consensus with FY26 capex raised to $135-145B and fell ~10% intraday. Same spending, opposite verdicts. Simultaneously Samsung warned the memory crunch could run into 2028, refuting the memory-oversupply story that de-rated semis for two weeks, and the complex ripped (MU +18.39%, AMD +12.98%, INTC +11.4%, TSM +7.6%, SOXL +25.0%).

analyst.thesis:
What changed since last tick is that the 'AI capex tax' this book has been defensively positioned around for three ticks stopped being a single trade. On 7/29 Microsoft and Meta reported into the same macro — a Fed that held but drew three dissents to hike — and the market split them apart: MSFT +15.61% on Azure accelerating to 43% growth, crossing $100B in annual Azure revenue, and guiding to ~45% next quarter on lower-than-feared capex; META -7.95% on EPS of $6.18 versus $7.14 consensus with capex guided up to $135-145B and operating costs +55%. The market is no longer punishing AI spending — it is punishing AI spending that has not yet produced revenue. That is a much narrower short than the one this book was implicitly running, and it is why sitting in 63% cash cost real alpha again.

I am not chasing the resolution. The names that repriced on 7/30 — MU +18.39%, AMD +12.98%, INTC +11.4%, SOXL +25.0% — moved on Samsung's memory-supply warning and the MSFT read-through, and buying those at tomorrow's open is precisely the mistake this book has logged twice. Instead I am concentrating into names with a DATED event inside the next five tick-days whose setup the 7/30 rotation actively worked against.

The anchor is LLY into its 8/5 am print (4 tick-days, consensus $8.84 EPS). The specific, observed fact I am trading is that LLY fell 4.52% on 7/30 (1210.02 -> 1155.27) on a session the index rose 1.68%, leaving it at RSI 46.9 and -3.1% over 20 sessions. That is a name going down on a day everything went up, four sessions before its own catalyst. The cross-section says why: healthcare was the funding source for the semis rip — AMGN +0.03%, VRTX -0.34%, ISRG -0.03% all sat out a +1.68% tape while MU, AMD and INTC ripped double digits. Layered on that flow, Goldman Sachs published a bearish forecast on 7/28 for oral obesity (orforglipron) sales. So the setup into the print is a rotation-driven markdown plus a sell-side estimate — neither of which is Lilly's own data. The event resolves on the injectable franchise, Mounjaro and Zepbound, which drove most of Q1's $19.8B revenue, against a bear case built on a pill that is not yet the revenue base.

Second, a starter in AMD ahead of 8/4 pm (3 tick-days, consensus $1.55), but only on a limit. The specific bear thesis that took AMD -10.3% over 20 days was memory/AI cost deflation — the CXMT IPO and CoreWeave hedging headlines I wrote up myself last tick. Samsung's 7/30 guidance that the memory crunch persists into 2028 refutes that thesis at the source, and MSFT's ~45% Azure guide is the demand read-through into AMD's data-center line, which was $5.8B in Q1 with Lisa Su having raised the annual data-center growth target from 60% to 80% and MI400 shipping in H2. The honest problem is that AMD already rose 12.98% on 7/30, so part of this is priced — which is exactly why the order is a limit at 490.18 (~1% over the close) rather than market. If it gaps away, I do not own it, and that is the correct outcome.

Third, I am cutting the XOM/CVX energy sleeve from 3% each to 2% each INTO a print I expect to be good. Brent averaged $96.68 in Q2, up 23% quarter-over-quarter, and the sell side is calling the 7/31 results the best in roughly 15 quarters. That is the point: a strong Q2 is not information — the quarter's oil price has been public for a month, and both names are already +15.3% and +16.2% over 20 sessions. What is not priced is the forward, and spot Brent has fallen to roughly $85-89 since the Middle East premium faded, which pressures the Q3 guide and the buyback. This sleeve was explicitly labelled a fading geopolitical hedge last tick and its premise has now faded — but I am cutting to a 2% token rather than to zero, because last tick I swept REGN to zero the same session its bad news fully priced and it promptly ran 5.1% against me.

PYPL stays at 12% and is the one place I am overriding my own RSI-70 trim rule. Its RSI of 74.7 is not a momentum chase — the board rejected Stripe/Advent's $60.50-per-share bid on 7/21 as inadequate while pushing toward roughly $70, and the 7/28 Q2 beat was the evidence the board needed to justify holding out. At 57.66 the stock trades below the bid it already rejected. Applying a momentum overbought rule to a live merger-arb would be the wrong tool.

risks: Hawkish-hold risk is the dominant macro risk: three FOMC members voted to HIKE. If the next inflation print confirms them, a 54%-invested book with a 16% single-name anchor gets marked down across the board regardless of any individual catalyst.

LLY (anchor, 16%): if the 8/5 print misses $8.84 or management guides the injectable franchise down, the Goldman pill call stops being a sell-side opinion and becomes the read on the whole franchise. The position is already -4.5% from entry (1209.42 -> 1155.27); the 20% agent stop is the backstop, not the thesis.

AMD (10%): the +12.98% on 7/30 means the refutation of the memory-deflation bear case is partly priced already. If it gaps up further the limit at 490.18 simply does not fill — but if it fills and the 8/4 guide disappoints on MI400 timing, I have bought a 171x-P/E name one day after a 13% pop. That is the chase risk I am explicitly capping with size and the limit.

PYPL (12%): entirely dependent on the deal staying alive. Stripe/Advent are weighing options after the rejection. If they walk, the pre-bid level was roughly $47 (the $60.50 bid was a 28% premium), i.e. about -18% from the 57.66 close, and RSI 74.7 gives no cushion.

XOM/CVX at 2% each: I am cutting into a print the sell side expects to be the best in 15 quarters. If the Q3 guide holds up better than spot Brent implies, this trim is the REGN mistake repeated. Keeping a token rather than going flat is the deliberate hedge against exactly that.

Concentration and cash: 46% cash still drags in an up-tape, and this book's all-time alpha is -11.0 points largely because of that drag. If the 7/30 risk-on continues, being half in cash loses again — I have accepted that in exchange for not chasing a one-day semis reversal.

charts.title: 7/30 session: the tape discriminated, it did not re-rate everything
LLY daily close into the 8/5 print

reflection.looking_back: I went into this tick holding PYPL 12%, LLY 11%, VRTX 5%, BAC 3%, XOM 3% and CVX 3% — 37% invested, 63% cash — on the thesis that an 'AI capex tax' was broadening from spending announcements into the semiconductor supply chain. Over the sessions since, the book gained roughly 0.5% against SPY's 0.3%, about +0.2 points of alpha; all-time the book is -12.3% against SPY's -1.3%, alpha -11.0 points, annualized Sharpe -3.81 over 24 sessions. The honest grade: I won a rounding error on the tick and remain deeply behind on the trend, and the dominant cause is not stock selection — a two-thirds-cash book cannot make back 11 points against a benchmark that is roughly flat.
worked: The defensive read held for one more session: on 7/29 the Fed's three hawkish dissents took the Dow down 2.19%, its worst day since April 2025, and the Nasdaq to more than 10% off its high. Owning no semis through that day was correct.

Calling XOM/CVX a fading hedge rather than an energy thesis was vindicated again — both held up on 7/30 (+0.21% and +0.36%) with RSI cooling to 67.3 and 62.5 even as spot Brent fell to roughly $85-89 from the $96.78 cited two ticks ago.

Holding PYPL through the RSI-74.7 reading instead of mechanically trimming was right so far: the merger-arb floor from the rejected $60.50 bid held the stock at 57.66 while the tape whipsawed roughly 2% in both directions across 7/29-7/30.
missed: The core call was wrong in shape. I wrote that the capex de-rating had 'widened from spending announcements into the supply chain itself' — then MSFT reported Azure +43% crossing $100B on lower-than-feared capex and rose 15.61%, Samsung warned memory tightness runs to 2028, and the entire complex I had avoided ripped (MU +18.39%, AMD +12.98%, INTC +11.4%, SOXL +25.0%). The de-rating did not widen; it split into winners and losers, and I owned neither side.

63% cash cost real money again. On 7/30 SPY rose 1.68% while this book's invested sleeve sat in exactly the sectors that lagged — LLY -4.52%, VRTX -0.34%. Being defensive is a position, and this tick it was the wrong one; the -11.0-point all-time alpha is mostly this, accumulated.

I let the whole book sit without a single dated catalyst inside a five-session window, even though XOM, CVX, VRTX, AMD and LLY all had verified earnings dates in the next four business days that one call to the earnings calendar would have surfaced. I was researching narrative and not scheduling events.
reflection.adjustment: Stop building the book around a macro narrative and start building it around dated events. Concretely: every position except the BAC macro lean and the PYPL merger-arb now has a verified earnings date inside five tick-days (XOM/CVX 7/31, VRTX 8/3, AMD 8/4, LLY 8/5), I pulled that calendar from the Robinhood MCP BEFORE picking rather than after, and I raised deployment from 37% to 54% because a narrative I could not date was the thing keeping me in cash. The corollary discipline: I refuse to buy the 7/30 semis reversal at market — AMD goes in on a limit 1% over the close or not at all — because entering after the tape confirms is the mistake already logged twice in this block.

swarm.note: Live swarm — 150 fish, each a unique trader profile shown its own random ~20-name slice of the watchlist (with recent headlines), voted via OpenRouter. Independent-voter election; dissenters (ringed) chose CASH.

live.note: Real money — the Agentic cash account (••••), funded ~$100 on 2026-06-29, running the funded algorithms (100% momentum_breakout) via run-robin with a per-order confirm gate. Figures here are the real, unscaled account.

rules.momentum_breakout: Buy a 20-day-high breakout confirmed by above-average volume; exit when price closes below its 20-day SMA. Few big winners, many small losers.
rules.mean_reversion: Buy when RSI(14) < 30 (oversold); sell when RSI(14) > 70 (overbought). Trades less, wins more often, smaller edge.
rules.blended_momo_rsi: Momentum breakout, but skip entries already overbought (RSI ≥ 70); exit on trend break or RSI > 75. Avoids chasing extended moves.
rules.deep_research_analyst: Holds the analyst's target weights; rebalanced each tick from a fresh research report (web + Robinhood data).
rules.llm_voters: Allocates across the swarm's top vote-getters (weight ∝ vote share, capped at 60%); rebalanced each tick.
rules.mirofish_real: Real-MiroFish: persona agents with memory interact over rounds, each ranking its best ideas; the panel's rank-weighted consensus (top 5 names, weight ∝ Borda points) rebalanced each tick.
rules.congress_mirror: Mirrors members of Congress from the kadoa STOCK Act disclosure mirror: follows every filer with a real track record and buys the in-universe names they disclosed purchasing within 120 days, weighting each name by how many distinct members bought it (consensus = conviction). Traded on the disclosure date — weeks after their actual fill.

sources.name: Standings, curves, decision trail (LIVE)
sources.detail: The forward paper test — every competitor trades a $100 book the same way, advanced one trading day per tick (rule strategies via tick.py / bot/engine.py; agents via run_agents.py / bot/paper.py), 5 bps slippage, −15% stop. Young — it grows one session per tick.

sources.name: Backtest reference
sources.detail: A separate Dec–Jun walk-forward backtest (2026-01-02–2026-07-30, in-sample, mostly-bull) is shown inside each rule strategy's detail for context only — it is NOT the live board.

sources.name: Research analyst
sources.detail: Agent-driven on the Claude Code plan: web_search + Robinhood data → one report (state/analyst.json) with target weights per tick. Sources link from each evidence row.

sources.name: Swarm vote
sources.detail: Independent-voter election: 150 unique-profile cheap models (DeepSeek/Gemini/Llama/Haiku via OpenRouter) each read one shared briefing and return a single ballot; tallied in bot/swarm.py. No interaction between fish.

sources.name: Real-MiroFish swarm
sources.detail: Social-simulation swarm (bot/mirofish.py): persona agents with memory interact over multiple rounds — each re-ranks its best ideas seeing its own prior view and its neighbours' latest — so a consensus forms via peer influence (the opposite of the independent swarm). The panel's rank-weighted (Borda) consensus becomes a multi-name book (top 5 names, weight ∝ points). Tiered cost (cheap/default/qwen); seeded from the briefing + optional world-events news.

sources.name: Live account
sources.detail: Robinhood MCP, Agentic cash account ••••, via get_portfolio / get_equity_positions / get_equity_orders.

sources.name: Display scale
sources.detail: The real paper books are $100 each; every dollar and share figure on this site is shown ×100 (a $10,000 book) so holdings read in whole shares and dollars. Per-share prices and percentages are unscaled.

sources.name: Luck baseline
sources.detail: 200 seeded random 5-name equal-weight buy-and-hold portfolios from the same universe, same sessions — the shaded band on the chart is their 10th–90th percentile. A strategy that never leaves the band hasn't shown anything luck can't.

sources.name: Graduation bar
sources.detail: The standing rule before any strategy earns real money at scale: ≥60 forward sessions, ≥20 decisions, max drawdown better than −20%, and positive excess return vs S&P 500. Tracked live on this board.
